proposals.evidence: DEDR1941: Malayalam ceṭi denotes shrub or small tree, Kannada ceṭṭu includes tree in general, and Telugu ceṭṭu denotes tree, plant, bush or creeper. Pattapu çedi fits this plant family with its palatal fricative and voiced non-retroflex stop retained. The source’s broad tree gloss is supported by members of the whole article even though Tamil ceṭi is glossed shrub/bush. Whole-article family membership is proposed; inheritance versus local transmission remains subject to review. This is a comparative family proposal; inheritance versus local transmission in this survey lect remains subject to review.

proposals.evidence: DEDR3610: Tamil/Malayalam nallatu means that which is good, Kodagu nallë means good, and Gondi (M.) nelā has an e-vowel. Pattapu nelid̪u is proposed within this nal-/nel- family with a final dental formation comparable to nallatu. Its vowels and single lateral remain explicit differences; no new suffix node or synchronic derivation is asserted. Whole-article family membership is proposed; inheritance versus local transmission remains subject to review. This is a comparative family proposal; inheritance versus local transmission in this survey lect remains subject to review.

proposals.evidence: DEDR4275: Tamil/Malayalam putu and Kota pud denote new; Kannada/Tulu posa show another medial consonant outcome in this family. Pattapu pucu retains the p-u stem but its medial c is not an exact match to the quoted forms. This qualified comparison requires review of the local palatal outcome and does not silently respell pucu as putu. Whole-article family membership is proposed; inheritance versus local transmission remains subject to review. Pattapu alāmu preserves the lateral-long-vowel-m formation with an initial a, a single lateral and final u. Those source differences remain explicit rather than normalizing the word to ellām. Whole-article family membership is proposed; inheritance versus local transmission remains subject to review.
